Since Bun 1.4.1, `fetch()` checks the server's certificate against the hostname in the URL. It used to take the name from a `Host` header.

The rule reports a request whose URL starts with `https://`. If it can't tell, it only reports a request that has `tls` options.

`bun lint --upgrade` runs this rule. See [Upgrade Bun](/lint#upgrade-bun).

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"bun/fetch-require-servername" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```ts
await fetch("https://10.0.0.5/", { headers: { Host: "internal.example" } });
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
await fetch("https://10.0.0.5/", {
  headers: { Host: "internal.example" },
  tls: { servername: "internal.example" },
});
await fetch("http://10.0.0.5/", { headers: { Host: "internal.example" } });
```
